Now, with regard to the Estafanama, the trial Court on consideration of the entire evidence on record found that it was not genuine and valid with regard to the question of possession, The trial Court came to a finding that the defendants were all along in possession of the suit-land, but the lower. appellate Court reversed the said finding of the trial Court and found that the surrender vide Ext. 4 was a genuine one and the same was followed by delivery of possession of the suit lands to landlords. Now, it is sericusly contended by the learned Advocate for the appellants that the trial Court on scrutiny of the evidence of both the sides held that there was no intention of the heirs of deceased Eusuf Ali to surrender the raiyati right in favour of the landlords and the alleged Estafanama was a false and fraudulent one. Firstly, for the reason that Sarbat Banu, the mother of defendant No. 1 who aIleged to have executed Estafanama on behalf of 2 other minors was an illiterate lady to whom the contents of the alleged Estafanama were not at all read over and explained in Bengali and now she has deposed in this suit as DW 4 and in her deposition, she has made her assertion and categorically stated that she did not surrender the suit-land and the alleged Estafanama was not read over and explained to her and as regards possessions she also stated that the defendants all-along were in possession and there was no delivery of possession in favour of the landlords after the so-called surrender. She has been corroborated by the evidence of other DWs, namely, DW 2 Fajool Mia and on the question of possession he has been also corroborated by other DWs. The lower appellate Court, it appears without considering the entire evidence on record with regard to surrender and possession of the suit lands and without adverting to the reasonings of the trial Court, wrongly found that Estafanama Ext. 4 to be genuine and found possession of the plaintiffs in the suit lands and illegally decreed the suit. 

 15. Now, in the light of the above decisions, it may be seen whether the learned Subordinate Judge rightly reversed the finding of the trial Court on the question of surrender and possession of the suit-lands on proper consideration of the evidence on record and in accordance with law. The learned Advocate for the appellants raised another very material question as to whether the provisions of section 86 of the Bengal Tenancy Act have been complied within making the alleged surrender by Estafanama Est. 4. Section 86 of the Bengal Tenancy Act provides for making surrender. 

 Of course, sub-section 7 of the said section, 86 of the Bengal Tenancy Act provides: 

 16. It is therefore contended by the learned Advocate for the appellants that there is nothing on record to show that the said provisions of law were complied with in making the alleged surrender vide Ext. 4. He also contends that admittedly defendant No.2 was alleged to have executed the Estafanama on behalf of the 2 minors and even the appellate Court also found that there could not be a legal and valid Estafanama on behalf of any minor and, as such, he left out 2 gondas share of the suit-land from the decree passed in favour of the plaintiff. The learned Advocate for the appellants contends that it appears that there was a partial surrender of the holding which is not permissible without complying with the provisions of section 86 of the Bengal Tenancy Act and as such the alleged surrender vide Ext. 4 was not legal and valid in the eye of law. In this connection he has referred to a decision in the case Sademani Sarder Vs. Mohammadali Mollah & others reported in 12 DLR 239 where-in it has been observed: 

 17. In order to constitute a valid surrender of a part of a holding under the Bengal Tenancy Act, the provisions of section 86 of the Bengal Tenancy Act must be complied with and there must be an arrangement between all the tenants and all the landlords to that effect. But in case of surrendering the entire holding which is governed by section 86(1) of the Act no consent of the landlord is necessary. 

 "A surrender is an yielding up of the term by the lessee to the person who has the right to re-enter, or in whom the immediate reversion expectant on the term is vested. In order to establish surrender by relinquishment of possession, the relinquishment must be in favour of the lessor, that is to say, a surrender may be implied from the fact that the lessee has permitted the lessor to re-enter and take over possession. It is, of course, not necessary that there must be, in every case, a physical taking over of possession but at least something amounting to a virtual taking over of possession must be proved, such as the lessee handing over the keys of the premises, to lessor, or the doing of some other act which would indicate a present intention to yield up the tenancy in favour of the lessor. To make out a case of abandonment, non-user must be accompanied by some other circumstance evidencing an intention to abandon. Similarly, for surrender also a mere relinquishment of the tenancy is not enough. A relinquishment without the making over of possession is not a valid surrender. The intention of the lessee must be the guiding factor is such case. Though this intention may be inferred from his actions A lease-hold interest being a heritable and, a transferable interest could be transferred to another person and, as such, the mere transfer of such an interest could not amount to an abandonment or relinquishment of the tenancy."
